shared_invariants: Rust owns authoritative game rules, state transitions, permissions, economy and persistence.
Next.js, React and TypeScript provide presentation only; Discord Activities use the official Embedded App SDK.
SQLite is the initial persistence target; do not add distributed infrastructure without measured need and an accepted decision.
Moonbits are earned-only, non-redeemable and never staked; all trade prices and rewards are disclosed.
No gambling, wagering, paid random rolls, paid loot boxes, cash-out or chance-based tradable rewards.
Healthy replayability comes from content, mastery, choice and cooperation; no punitive streaks, fake scarcity or pressure loops.
All public content is original or rights-cleared, moderated and age-appropriate.
Every node must support privacy inventory, data export/deletion coverage, accessible fallback and failure recovery.

domains.title: The Hearth and Tavern
domains.summary: The Tavern is Moonbyte's social home: the default place to discover activities, form parties, meet authored characters, review stories and step into the wider world.

connections.rationale: turns player needs and discovered demand into transparent Bazaar browsing
converts rumours, NPC conversations and notice-board entries into optional quest starts
provides immediate short-session games between longer adventures
gives friends and parties a shared meeting point without requiring a public conversation

domains.title: The Bazaar and Exchange
domains.summary: The Bazaar circulates earned goods through understandable fixed-price listings, barter and contracts. It is a utility for players, never a speculative or wagering market.

connections.rationale: makes stalls and requests discoverable from the Tavern rather than requiring users to memorise commands
connects player demand to published recipes, ingredient lists and crafting work orders
uses canonical item definitions and collection rules to determine what can be listed
uses atomic escrow, append-only receipts and deterministic ledger rules

domains.title: Guilds and Long-Form Cooperation
domains.summary: Guilds coordinate shared adventures, persistent projects and optional social identity while individual ownership and server boundaries remain explicit.

connections.rationale: binds guild identity and moderation to the correct Discord server
forms parties for map-based expeditions and cooperative routes
provides the membership and contribution model for Guild Vault challenges
turns verified participation and skill accomplishments into transparent guild recognition

domains.title: Server Culture and Community Layer
domains.summary: Every Discord guild can shape its own Moonbyte experience through scoped configuration, community content and moderation, while shared player identity remains separate.

connections.rationale: provides the Discord server boundary and permission context for guild features
turns server calendars into optional community events and celebrations
uses moderation, privacy and rate-limit policies for server-owned features
lets administrators choose which approved game categories appear in the server library

domains.title: Atlas, Regions and World Discovery
domains.summary: The Atlas provides a navigable world graph. Discovery is evidence-based, persistent and useful to quests, expeditions, collections and community maps.

connections.rationale: supplies destinations, distances, landmarks and route constraints for expeditions
turns discovered places and clues into optional story routes
stores discoveries, cartography and lore as durable collection entries
lets authored world events decorate or add content to known regions without removing access

domains.title: Expeditions and Exploration Sessions
domains.summary: Expeditions turn the Atlas into bounded, resumable adventures with cooperative roles, clear checkpoints and discovery-based results.

connections.rationale: selects known regions, routes, landmarks and environmental rules
routes suitable discoveries into puzzle chambers and structured challenge rooms
allows guilds to coordinate asynchronous contributions and party membership
turns discoveries, route notes and completed objectives into permanent entries

domains.title: Quests, Mystery and Story
domains.summary: Quests provide authored purpose across the Tavern, Atlas, Vaults, NPCs and guilds. Branches are visible, resumable and replayable.

connections.rationale: places every quest objective at a named region, route or landmark
lets quests culminate in structured puzzle or mastery spaces
rewards completed skill and understanding with transparent records
surfaces rumours and story contracts in a calm central hub

domains.title: Vaults, Dungeons and Puzzle Spaces
domains.summary: Vaults are designed challenge spaces with disclosed rules, fixed rewards, saved checkpoints and no paid or chance-based loot-box behaviour.

connections.rationale: provides authored quest objectives and narrative context for each challenge
connects known recipes and crafted tools to specific puzzle mechanics
uses reproducible transcripts for eligible randomised score-only elements while keeping rewards fixed
hosts shared roles and parallel clue paths for Guild Vaults

domains.title: Gathering, Crafting and Workshops
domains.summary: Crafting transforms known inputs into predictable outputs and links exploration, Bazaar demand, homes and collections. It is not a random loot system.

connections.rationale: fulfils wanted-board requests and work orders through known recipe outputs
uses stable item definitions, provenance and collection membership
turns crafted objects into useful home decorations and workshop upgrades
creates disclosed route kits and tools before an expedition begins

domains.title: Collections, Bestiary and Museum
domains.summary: The Archive preserves discoveries, lore and earned cosmetics. Collection completion is an expression of exploration and authorship, not a paid random chase.

connections.rationale: archives relics and challenge records produced by completed Vault rooms
turns verified location discoveries and cartography into permanent entries
maintains stable item and recipe identities with provenance
lets players exhibit earned collections in a personally controlled space

domains.title: Arcade and Original Mini-Games
domains.summary: The Arcade is a curated library of short, medium and mastery-based games. Results feed profiles and quests through explicit, bounded contracts.

connections.rationale: lets players start a short game from a Tavern table without navigating a separate service
creates personal records, practice paths and transparent skill achievements
documents random inputs and competitive scoring where verification is useful
supports friend challenges and shared play with clear exit and privacy controls

domains.title: Parties, Lobbies and Multiplayer Rules
domains.summary: Multiplayer uses one shared session contract for identity, turn ownership, deadlines, reconnects, spectators and host controls.

connections.rationale: allows guild members to coordinate long-running group activities
runs approved games through the same lobby and session engine
provides friend invitations, opt-in groups and cooperative roles
uses documented rules and verifiable transcripts for supported competitive outcomes

domains.title: Characters, Companions and Tactical Identity
domains.summary: Characters provide optional strategic identity and story expression. Power is earned predictably, cosmetic choices stay cosmetic and companions are original.

connections.rationale: uses transparent practice and achievements to unlock documented character options
gives parties complementary utility without requiring one optimal composition
uses known recipes and item definitions for non-random equipment
connects character choices to authored story dialogue and branch flags

domains.title: Progression, Mastery and Recognition
domains.summary: Progression recognises real accomplishments using clear thresholds. It never depends on daily attendance, spending or hidden random reward rolls.

connections.rationale: uses game results and practice lessons as skill evidence
provides predictable side-grade character and utility milestones
stores achievements, personal records and earned recognition
supports optional guild recognition for contribution and cooperation

domains.title: Festivals, Chapters and World Events
domains.summary: Events are authored content windows and celebrations, not scarcity traps. Core rewards and story access remain available through archives or repeat routes.

connections.rationale: uses community calendars and guild preferences for event planning
gives guilds cooperative roles in festivals and world-building
adds visible decorations, dialogues and optional puzzles to known regions
surfaces a festival calmly through the Tavern and player-selected digests

domains.title: Homes, Gardens and Personal Spaces
domains.summary: Homes are expressive personal spaces where players display earned discoveries and craft decorations. Visiting and sharing are opt-in.

connections.rationale: uses crafted objects and workshop recipes as home furnishings
allows players to exhibit earned collection entries and curated sets
supports opt-in friend visits and party gatherings
allows optional shared guild rooms and community displays

domains.title: Player Creation and Community Content
domains.summary: Creation tools use constrained templates, provenance, moderation and reproducible tests. Original work can be shared, but no user submission silently becomes trusted game logic.

connections.rationale: applies reporting, review, permissions and privacy policy to player-submitted material
allows approved puzzle packs and variants to appear in the curated game library
supports authored side stories and scenario prompts through bounded dialogue templates
stores approved community works and their creators with explicit visibility

domains.title: Fair Play, Competition and Verification
domains.summary: Fairness provides deterministic rules, auditable outcomes and honest scoreboards. It never converts chance into tradable value or a wager.

connections.rationale: ensures turn order, scoring and participant contributions are reproducible
uses atomic ledgers and receipts for every trade and escrow transition
allows players to reproduce relevant game results and puzzle score calculations
keeps challenge generation and fixed rewards auditable

domains.title: Friends, Community Bonds and Social Play
domains.summary: Social systems help people cooperate, create and remember shared moments. They remain consent-based, scoped and easy to mute or leave.

connections.rationale: uses the Tavern as a familiar shared meeting point
lets friends form or join structured long-running groups
uses the universal lobby, turn and reconnect contracts
connects shared milestones to optional community events

domains.title: Accessibility, Moderation, Privacy and Operations
domains.summary: Trust systems are cross-cutting foundations: accessible controls, safe content, privacy boundaries, reliable delivery and transparent operations apply to every game.

connections.rationale: enforces guild configuration, channel scope and moderator permissions
validates player-generated material before public distribution
provides integrity, appeal and result-verification processes
exposes privacy, accessibility and notification settings from the central hub

nodes.title: The Lantern and Ladle
nodes.summary: A persistent, recognisable social home where every player can see what is available without searching a command catalogue.
nodes.purpose: It replaces disconnected entry commands with one navigable place and establishes the tone of the world.
nodes.player_loop: Arrive, inspect the room, choose a table or notice, invite a party, then leave or continue into a destination.
nodes.output: A clear next-action menu, a resumable home location and a shared visual identity.

nodes.title: The Notice Wall
nodes.summary: A readable wall that gathers quests, guild requests, player commissions, community projects and server announcements into one filtered board.
nodes.purpose: It prevents important activities from being buried in chat and makes the world feel connected without constant notifications.
nodes.player_loop: Open the wall, filter by category and time expectation, inspect terms, pin an activity to a personal route, then accept or dismiss it.
nodes.output: A selected activity and a saved route; dismissing an entry never penalises the player.

nodes.title: The Rumour Circle
nodes.summary: A narrative discovery surface where authored rumours hint at places, NPCs, puzzles and world history rather than hiding random prizes.
nodes.purpose: It links Tavern social play to exploration and gives players reasons to compare clues and form hypotheses.
nodes.player_loop: Hear a rumour, inspect its evidence level, ask a follow-up, compare it with the Atlas, then choose whether to investigate.
nodes.output: Clue references, world knowledge flags and optional quest leads.

nodes.title: The Common Tables
nodes.summary: A set of named tables for quick solo, cooperative and party games with clear session lengths and player limits.
nodes.purpose: It gives the social hub a low-friction arcade entrance while preserving the separate game-session contract.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a table, preview rules, invite or queue with friends, play a bounded round, then review the result.
nodes.output: A completed mini-game session, personal record and optional progression event.

nodes.title: The Host's Bench
nodes.summary: A lobby desk for creating a hosted activity, choosing visibility, setting seat limits and managing invitations.
nodes.purpose: It unifies lobbies across games instead of implementing a different invitation pattern in every module.
nodes.player_loop: Select an activity, set a public or private room, preview permissions, invite participants, ready the group and launch.
nodes.output: A validated lobby with host authority, join history and a recoverable session identity.

nodes.title: The Story Stage
nodes.summary: A moderated space for original player-written tales, riddles, recaps and short performances connected to places in the world.
nodes.purpose: It creates community expression without copying protected songs, characters or third-party stories.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a prompt, compose original text, preview formatting, submit for display, receive reactions and archive the work.
nodes.output: Attributed creative entries, reviewed display status and links to the world nodes they reference.

nodes.title: The Hearth Kitchen
nodes.summary: A cooperative recipe and cooking station where ingredients earned through play become known dishes, buffs for puzzles or decorative table items.
nodes.purpose: It turns gathering and crafting into a social activity and gives the Tavern a useful sink for non-premium resources.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect recipes, contribute known ingredients, prepare a deterministic result, share servings and save the recipe.
nodes.output: A crafted dish with published effects, ingredient provenance and an optional shared-session benefit.

nodes.title: The Regulars' Circle
nodes.summary: A roster of authored Tavern NPCs whose dialogue reflects world events, completed chapters and the player's chosen interests.
nodes.purpose: It makes narrative state visible through a warm hub while avoiding randomised affection or manipulative character timers.
nodes.player_loop: Meet a regular, select a dialogue topic, receive a clue or story response, unlock a journal note and return later.
nodes.output: Dialogue flags, character lore entries and contextual leads.

nodes.title: The Common Room Project
nodes.summary: A cooperative decoration plan that lets a server vote on and contribute to permanent Tavern improvements.
nodes.purpose: It creates a shared goal whose output is visible to everyone and does not require daily check-ins.
nodes.player_loop: Review a published renovation plan, choose a contribution, add earned materials, inspect progress and vote on a completed design.
nodes.output: A permanent room upgrade, contribution record and new optional interaction point.

nodes.title: The Tavern Wayfinder
nodes.summary: A contextual navigation panel that remembers a player's preferred destinations and shows useful next steps from the hub.
nodes.purpose: It reduces command friction and lets a very large game remain understandable from Discord.
nodes.player_loop: Open the wayfinder, choose a destination, inspect its prerequisites, pin or launch it, then return to the same hub context.
nodes.output: Saved navigation preferences and consistent deep links into the shared world graph.

nodes.title: Player Stallfronts
nodes.summary: Each player can operate a small, customisable stall that presents eligible goods, fixed prices and a short description.
nodes.purpose: It gives trading a social identity while keeping the transaction model simple and inspectable.
nodes.player_loop: Create a stall, choose a permitted theme, select eligible stock, publish listings, answer requests and manage completed orders.
nodes.output: A discoverable storefront, active listing set and stall history.

nodes.title: Fixed-Price Listings
nodes.summary: Every listing states one exact item, quantity, total price, expiry and seller before a buyer commits.
nodes.purpose: It removes hidden pricing, bid pressure and speculative auction behaviour from the economy.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect the item, check seller and total, confirm purchase, receive a receipt and see the inventory update.
nodes.output: An atomic trade record and a deterministic transfer of item and Moonbits.

nodes.title: The Barter Desk
nodes.summary: Players can propose a transparent exchange of named items and optional Moonbits with both sides seeing the complete offer.
nodes.purpose: It supports flexible trading without hidden valuations or gambling-like bid mechanics.
nodes.player_loop: Select owned eligible items, build an offer, send it privately, inspect the counter-offer and confirm both sides.
nodes.output: A bilateral trade proposal with expiry, escrow and a signed-in-system receipt.

nodes.title: The Wanted Board
nodes.summary: Buyers post specific requests with desired quantities, accepted variants and a maximum disclosed price.
nodes.purpose: It makes the Bazaar demand-led and connects collectors, crafters and explorers.
nodes.player_loop: Create a request, publish constraints, receive matching offers, compare provenance and accept one complete offer.
nodes.output: A fulfilled request, request status and a traceable connection to the source activity.

nodes.title: Crafting Work Orders
nodes.summary: A buyer commissions a known recipe from a crafter using published inputs, fixed compensation and a delivery deadline chosen by agreement.
nodes.purpose: It turns crafting into a community service rather than a random loot chase.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a recipe, agree inputs and price, reserve materials, craft the item, deliver and release escrow.
nodes.output: A completed commission, recipe version, material provenance and clear settlement.

nodes.title: The Price Reference Ledger
nodes.summary: A non-speculative reference view summarises recent completed fixed-price trades and marks small samples clearly.
nodes.purpose: It helps players understand ordinary prices without presenting items as investments.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect a stable item definition, view completed-trade bands, check sample size and return to the actual listing.
nodes.output: Aggregate reference information with privacy-safe counts and explicit uncertainty.

nodes.title: The Escrow Vault
nodes.summary: A transaction state machine reserves goods and currency during a trade, then commits or refunds everything exactly once.
nodes.purpose: It protects both parties from duplicate clicks, disconnects and concurrent purchases.
nodes.player_loop: Create an offer, reserve the exact assets, confirm both parties, atomically commit or expire and refund.
nodes.output: A recoverable escrow record and an immutable trade receipt.

nodes.title: Item Provenance Cards
nodes.summary: Each eligible item can show its origin, definition version, craft recipe and earned history without exposing private player data.
nodes.purpose: It makes ownership trustworthy and allows trade eligibility to be explained.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect an item card, read its source, check restrictions, view public-safe history and list or keep it.
nodes.output: A provenance chain attached to the stable item identity.

nodes.title: The Delivery Board
nodes.summary: A fulfilment queue tracks accepted orders, delivery state, collection points and expiry without requiring players to stay online.
nodes.purpose: It completes the market loop for commissions and asynchronous trades.
nodes.player_loop: Accept an order, fulfil the listed conditions, mark ready, let the receiver claim it and archive the receipt.
nodes.output: A deterministic delivery state with a clear pickup or cancellation path.

nodes.title: The Trade Review Desk
nodes.summary: A bounded dispute workflow lets users report an incorrect fulfilment and gives moderators an evidence-only review view.
nodes.purpose: It provides recourse without making informal moderator judgement part of normal transaction execution.
nodes.player_loop: Open a receipt, choose a factual issue, attach allowed evidence references, receive a review state and see the resolution.
nodes.output: A private case record, moderator outcome and audited correction if one is justified.

nodes.title: Guild Charters
nodes.summary: A guild begins with a clear purpose, membership rules, privacy settings and a visible list of shared goals.
nodes.purpose: It creates a real community structure rather than a cosmetic tag attached to a leaderboard.
nodes.player_loop: Draft a charter, preview permissions, invite members, record agreement and publish the guild identity.
nodes.output: A versioned guild charter and a recoverable membership boundary.

nodes.title: The Guild Hall
nodes.summary: Each guild gets a shared visual hall with its banner, current project, member roles, notices and recent public achievements.
nodes.purpose: It gives members one coherent place to coordinate without exposing private player inventories.
nodes.player_loop: Open the hall, inspect its boards, choose a project, view allowed member details and return to a party or world area.
nodes.output: A guild-scoped view model and persistent hall configuration.

nodes.title: Guild Role Charter
nodes.summary: Guild leaders can define bounded roles such as organiser, builder, archivist and moderator with specific permissions.
nodes.purpose: It limits arbitrary power and makes responsibilities understandable to members.
nodes.player_loop: Review a role template, assign a member, preview permitted actions, audit changes and revoke access when needed.
nodes.output: A least-privilege role assignment and auditable permission history.

nodes.title: The Great Works Board
nodes.summary: Guild members jointly complete long-term construction, mapping, archive or puzzle projects with visible contribution categories.
nodes.purpose: It gives cooperation a meaningful output that persists beyond one match.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a work, inspect required contributions, complete one task, review team progress and vote on the finished result.
nodes.output: A guild project state, contribution ledger and world-visible completion.

nodes.title: Guild Story Contracts
nodes.summary: A shared quest line lets a guild divide puzzle, exploration and crafting objectives without forcing everyone to be online together.
nodes.purpose: It combines individual play sessions into one authored group story.
nodes.player_loop: Accept the contract, assign optional branches, submit independently earned evidence and resolve the final shared objective.
nodes.output: A quest graph with contribution attribution and idempotent rewards.

nodes.title: The Guild Vault
nodes.summary: A cooperative challenge instance contains parallel clues, shared rooms and role-specific tasks whose rewards are known before entry.
nodes.purpose: It makes the Vault system a social puzzle rather than a lottery chest.
nodes.player_loop: Preview the vault, form a party, distribute clues, coordinate actions, save checkpoints and claim the fixed result.
nodes.output: A guild-scoped vault run with validated contribution and fixed rewards.

nodes.title: The Guild Cartography Room
nodes.summary: Members can annotate a shared map with verified discoveries, routes and authored notes subject to moderation.
nodes.purpose: It makes exploration useful to the whole group while separating verified facts from speculation.
nodes.player_loop: Open a region, add a private draft note, attach an evidence reference, submit it, then publish after review.
nodes.output: A shared map layer with revision history and contributor attribution.

nodes.title: Guild Neighbourhoods
nodes.summary: Two or more guilds can opt into a bounded cooperative event or shared puzzle without merging their private data.
nodes.purpose: It supports cross-server community without building a global unrestricted social graph.
nodes.player_loop: Invite another guild, review the event's public scope, accept the collaboration, complete shared tasks and close the link.
nodes.output: A time-bounded collaboration contract with explicit visibility and separate ledgers.

nodes.title: Guild Trust Record
nodes.summary: A transparent record tracks fulfilled commitments, moderation standing and cooperative milestones rather than traded power.
nodes.purpose: It gives members context for collaboration without creating a pay-to-win ranking.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect evidence-backed milestones, view the rules, submit a correction request and compare only like-for-like records.
nodes.output: A public-safe reputation summary that cannot be purchased or transferred.

nodes.title: The Guild Chronicle
nodes.summary: The guild can preserve completed projects, expedition maps, event memories and authored recaps as a searchable shared archive.
nodes.purpose: It makes long-form group work matter after the immediate reward is claimed.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a completed record, approve its display scope, add an original recap and link its map or quest references.
nodes.output: A durable guild chronicle entry with privacy-aware authorship.

nodes.title: Server World Identity
nodes.summary: A guild can choose its own nameplate, colour palette from approved art, welcome scene and enabled game categories.
nodes.purpose: It makes different servers feel distinct without forking the global rules or item definitions.
nodes.player_loop: Authorised admin opens server settings, previews a theme, chooses enabled content and publishes the configuration.
nodes.output: A guild-scoped configuration version and presentation theme.

nodes.title: Community Calendar
nodes.summary: A calendar lists opt-in sessions, guild projects, puzzle nights and authored festivals with clear time zones and RSVP controls.
nodes.purpose: It coordinates real people without turning attendance into a reward obligation.
nodes.player_loop: Browse the calendar, inspect duration and access, RSVP, receive only opted-in reminders and cancel freely.
nodes.output: A scheduled activity, RSVP list and bounded notification plan.

nodes.title: Channel Wayfinding
nodes.summary: Admins can map activity types to appropriate channels and set whether boards are public, private or ephemeral.
nodes.purpose: It keeps public games tidy and prevents personal information from spilling into public channels.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a category, select permitted channels, preview message visibility and save a versioned route.
nodes.output: A channel policy that the bot checks before publishing.

nodes.title: Server Challenge Board
nodes.summary: A server can host optional shared challenges with one clear objective, one end condition and a published contribution rule.
nodes.purpose: It creates community play without competitive pressure or punitive streaks.
nodes.player_loop: Read the challenge, join explicitly, contribute a valid action, inspect shared progress and leave at any time.
nodes.output: A guild-scoped challenge state and non-random, published completion result.

nodes.title: The Community Museum
nodes.summary: A server may curate approved public artwork, puzzle solutions, map discoveries and event recaps into a browsable gallery.
nodes.purpose: It celebrates community creation while keeping publication permission explicit.
nodes.player_loop: Submit an entry, choose its visibility, pass review, place it in a gallery and allow the creator to request removal.
nodes.output: A moderated gallery item with attribution and revision state.

nodes.title: Neighbourhood Goals
nodes.summary: Members contribute to a server-wide build or discovery milestone that unlocks a permanent shared decoration or archive entry.
nodes.purpose: It turns cooperation into a visible result instead of a temporary ranking race.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect the goal, choose one contribution type, submit evidence, review milestones and celebrate completion.
nodes.output: A permanent shared outcome with no decay if the server is quiet.

nodes.title: Scoped Scoreboards
nodes.summary: Administrators can enable opt-in leaderboards for supported games with clear windows, tie rules and privacy-safe display names.
nodes.purpose: It supports friendly competition without turning every activity into a global status contest.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a game and scope, read scoring rules, opt in, inspect records and hide personal display from the board.
nodes.output: A guild-scoped, rules-versioned ranking snapshot.

nodes.title: Server Steward Desk
nodes.summary: Moderators receive tools for reports, content review, channel restrictions and event pauses without access to private player records.
nodes.purpose: It keeps community safety independent from the game's economic and progression logic.
nodes.player_loop: Open a report queue, inspect minimum necessary evidence, choose a bounded action and record a reason.
nodes.output: An auditable moderation action with least-privilege access.

nodes.title: Server Data Boundary
nodes.summary: The server layer documents which settings belong to a guild and which data remains player-owned across all servers.
nodes.purpose: It prevents accidental cross-guild disclosure and makes privacy controls understandable.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect data categories, review a guild setting, change a consent or visibility value and verify the scope.
nodes.output: A data-boundary inventory and isolation test contract.

nodes.title: The Quiet Community Digest
nodes.summary: An opt-in digest summarises important completed projects and upcoming events at a chosen frequency without activity bait.
nodes.purpose: It keeps members informed without ping floods, urgency language or daily pressure.
nodes.player_loop: Choose digest topics, frequency and delivery channel, preview content and pause or opt out at any time.
nodes.output: A small scheduled summary generated from public-safe events.

nodes.title: The Grand Atlas
nodes.summary: A canonical world map links regions, settlements, landmarks, routes and story chapters through stable IDs.
nodes.purpose: It gives every feature a common place reference and prevents disconnected content lists.
nodes.player_loop: Open the Atlas, choose a region, inspect its known routes, pin a destination and launch a compatible activity.
nodes.output: A world graph and stable location IDs shared across game modules.

nodes.title: Discovery Layers
nodes.summary: A map distinguishes unknown, rumoured, visited and verified locations without hiding essential rules behind random rolls.
nodes.purpose: It makes exploration meaningful while keeping players aware of what is speculation and what is confirmed.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect a region, choose a lead, visit through a supported activity, verify evidence and update the map layer.
nodes.output: A player-specific discovery state and optional public-safe map contribution.

nodes.title: Biome Ecology
nodes.summary: Each region has an authored visual palette, puzzle vocabulary, resources, NPC roles and environmental mechanics.
nodes.purpose: It makes locations mechanically distinct instead of changing only the background image.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a biome, learn its rules, encounter its resource and puzzle types, then carry discoveries into crafting or story.
nodes.output: Versioned biome definitions and reusable environment rules.

nodes.title: Landmark Network
nodes.summary: Landmarks act as stable navigation anchors with lore, nearby challenges, access notes and shared map references.
nodes.purpose: It gives players memorable destinations and makes directions easy to discuss in Discord.
nodes.player_loop: Select a landmark, read its context, follow a route, complete an optional interaction and save the discovery.
nodes.output: Landmark state, route references and an archive record.

nodes.title: Known Passage Network
nodes.summary: Verified shortcuts connect previously explored locations and remove repetitive navigation steps.
nodes.purpose: It rewards knowledge and makes return trips faster without selling travel or requiring a timer.
nodes.player_loop: Discover a passage, solve or fulfil its published requirement, confirm both endpoints and use it in later routes.
nodes.output: A validated edge in the world graph with no hidden random travel outcome.

nodes.title: Environmental Logic Sites
nodes.summary: Some landmarks contain local puzzles that use the shape, order, symbols or history of the region.
nodes.purpose: It makes the world itself playable and feeds puzzle knowledge into the wider quest graph.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect environmental clues, collect evidence, test an allowed hypothesis, solve and record the method.
nodes.output: A solved site state and an optional explanation for future players.

nodes.title: Atlas Overlays
nodes.summary: Players can switch between routes, resources, story clues, public guild notes and personal pins without mixing their visibility.
nodes.purpose: It makes a dense world readable and prevents private notes from becoming public by default.
nodes.player_loop: Select a layer, filter symbols, inspect provenance and choose whether a note is personal, party or guild-visible.
nodes.output: Separate versioned map layers and safe display metadata.

nodes.title: Cartographer's Desk
nodes.summary: Players can turn verified discoveries into clean maps, route guides and original annotations for other explorers.
nodes.purpose: It creates a meaningful knowledge role and connects exploration to community authorship.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a region, select verified points, arrange a route, add original notes, preview and publish at a chosen scope.
nodes.output: A versioned cartographic work with source references.

nodes.title: The Route Planner
nodes.summary: A route planner estimates step count, puzzle difficulty and expected session time across known destinations.
nodes.purpose: It helps players choose an adventure that fits their available time without forcing a long session.
nodes.player_loop: Choose start and destination, apply party filters, preview route costs and hazards, then launch or save.
nodes.output: A route proposal with explicit assumptions and no real-time travel pressure.

nodes.title: Living World State
nodes.summary: Authored global chapter flags can alter region descriptions, NPC dialogue and available puzzles while preserving completed content.
nodes.purpose: It creates a world that evolves through story outcomes rather than time-limited scarcity.
nodes.player_loop: Read a chapter outcome, inspect the change log, visit an affected region and interact with its new state.
nodes.output: Versioned world-state events with deterministic migrations and archival access.

nodes.title: Expedition Planner
nodes.summary: A party chooses a destination, route, difficulty, session length and optional objectives before the journey begins.
nodes.purpose: It converts open-world exploration into a bounded activity suitable for Discord interactions.
nodes.player_loop: Select a destination, preview route and risks, invite party members, choose roles and confirm the plan.
nodes.output: A versioned expedition plan with clear membership and estimated duration.

nodes.title: Route Encounters
nodes.summary: Routes contain authored riddles, environmental obstacles, navigation choices and non-graphic turn-based encounters.
nodes.purpose: It gives travel decisions a gameplay purpose without requiring real-time input or violent spectacle.
nodes.player_loop: Reach a route node, inspect the challenge, choose a legal party action, resolve it and continue or retreat.
nodes.output: A resolved route node and an explanation of the outcome.

nodes.title: Expedition Roles
nodes.summary: Players select complementary roles such as Scout, Scholar, Navigator or Maker that expose different useful actions.
nodes.purpose: It rewards coordination and knowledge rather than requiring one player to dominate every activity.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a role, inspect its allowed actions, contribute during the matching phase and change roles between runs.
nodes.output: A party role assignment and clear action permissions.

nodes.title: Prepared Supply Kit
nodes.summary: Players assemble a visible kit from earned, non-premium materials with exact effects stated before departure.
nodes.purpose: It links crafting and planning while keeping item consumption predictable.
nodes.player_loop: Review a route's supply requirements, select owned items, confirm the kit and see the planned use for each item.
nodes.output: A locked loadout snapshot with item provenance and deterministic use rules.

nodes.title: Waystation Checkpoints
nodes.summary: Waystations let a party save its current route node, review progress and leave without losing completed objectives.
nodes.purpose: It makes longer play respectful of real schedules and Discord disconnects.
nodes.player_loop: Reach a checkpoint, inspect the saved state, choose continue, pause or leave, then resume from the exact checkpoint.
nodes.output: A recoverable expedition checkpoint with idempotent progress.

nodes.title: The Expedition Journal
nodes.summary: A journal assembles route decisions, clues, discovered landmarks and party contributions into a readable recap.
nodes.purpose: It makes each run useful even when the party does not complete every optional objective.
nodes.player_loop: Record an event, attach a map point, add an original note, choose visibility and review the finished log.
nodes.output: A structured private, party or guild journal entry.

nodes.title: Return and Recovery Routes
nodes.summary: A party that pauses or withdraws receives a clear return route and keeps every already completed objective.
nodes.purpose: It prevents a failed or interrupted expedition from confiscating unrelated progress.
nodes.player_loop: Choose to withdraw, review saved milestones, close active phases and return to the last safe hub.
nodes.output: A clean session end state and preserved completed discoveries.

nodes.title: Explorer Contracts
nodes.summary: An optional contract asks a party to document a specific route, solve a local puzzle or catalogue an authored discovery.
nodes.purpose: It gives each expedition a clear purpose and feeds verified knowledge back to the world.
nodes.player_loop: Read the objective and reward, attach a suitable route, complete it, submit evidence and collect the fixed result.
nodes.output: A contract record linked to the Atlas and player or guild progress.

nodes.title: Discovery Scorecard
nodes.summary: A scorecard recognises clue quality, optional objectives, teamwork and route efficiency with transparent scoring rules.
nodes.purpose: It supports mastery without rewarding excessive session length or random loot.
nodes.player_loop: Finish an expedition, inspect each scoring component, compare the rules version and save a personal record.
nodes.output: A deterministic score and contribution summary.

nodes.title: Expedition Route Archive
nodes.summary: Completed routes can be replayed with altered authored objectives or difficulty while preserving the original discovery record.
nodes.purpose: It supports learning and group play without disguising repetition as new content.
nodes.player_loop: Select an archived route, choose a published variant, start a fresh run and compare results.
nodes.output: A new run linked to the original route version.

nodes.title: The Quest Board
nodes.summary: A curated board groups story chapters, side stories, guild requests and puzzles by topic and expected time.
nodes.purpose: It makes the world's activity legible instead of turning quests into an endless notification stream.
nodes.player_loop: Browse categories, inspect prerequisites and fixed rewards, pin an objective and accept it when ready.
nodes.output: A player-owned quest state with visible conditions and no hidden timers.

nodes.title: Chapter Arcs
nodes.summary: A chapter arc links multiple short quests into one story with checkpoints and clearly described completion conditions.
nodes.purpose: It creates continuity across sessions without requiring a player to be online at a specific hour.
nodes.player_loop: Read the chapter summary, choose an available branch, complete an objective, save and resume the next chapter.
nodes.output: A versioned narrative graph and durable checkpoint.

nodes.title: Choice and Consequence Graph
nodes.summary: Important story decisions change later dialogue, available routes and archive summaries through authored rules.
nodes.purpose: It gives players agency without secretly changing reward odds or punishing a non-optimal choice.
nodes.player_loop: Review the choice context, inspect known consequences where appropriate, select an option and record the branch.
nodes.output: A persistent branch flag with replay-safe consequences.

nodes.title: The Investigation Desk
nodes.summary: Mystery quests combine evidence cards, map references, NPC statements and deduction boards into a solvable case.
nodes.purpose: It links social rumour, exploration and puzzle systems in a coherent detective experience.
nodes.player_loop: Collect evidence, compare sources, form a hypothesis, test it against the rules and submit a conclusion.
nodes.output: An evidence graph, hypothesis history and verified solution result.

nodes.title: Dialogue Routes
nodes.summary: NPC conversations expose topic-based dialogue nodes that react to completed story flags and the player's selected approach.
nodes.purpose: It makes character writing part of the game engine rather than hard-coded command text.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a topic, inspect available responses, make a narrative choice and unlock the relevant follow-up.
nodes.output: A versioned dialogue node and associated story flags.

nodes.title: Faction Storylines
nodes.summary: Several authored factions offer parallel narratives and useful world services without requiring allegiance for basic play.
nodes.purpose: It provides long-term narrative choice without locking players out of core content.
nodes.player_loop: Read each faction's values, complete an introductory task, choose optional cooperation and track consequences.
nodes.output: Faction state and clearly scoped rewards or dialogue changes.

nodes.title: Local Tales
nodes.summary: Small stories attached to a landmark, item, guild member or tavern regular provide self-contained adventures.
nodes.purpose: It ensures a player can have a satisfying short session without committing to a chapter arc.
nodes.player_loop: Find a lead, read the setup, solve one or more compact objectives and archive the ending.
nodes.output: A complete short narrative record.

nodes.title: Shared Story Decisions
nodes.summary: A party can pool clues and make one agreed story decision with each participant seeing the same outcome and contribution summary.
nodes.purpose: It makes collaborative storytelling a first-class multiplayer mode.
nodes.player_loop: Create a shared chapter, gather private or public clues, vote under clear rules and commit one final choice.
nodes.output: A party-owned branch with contribution attribution.

nodes.title: The Chapter Chronicle
nodes.summary: A searchable archive records completed branches, important clues, character appearances and world-state changes.
nodes.purpose: It helps players remember the story and supports returning after a long pause.
nodes.player_loop: Open a chapter, filter its entries, inspect source links and resume from an available checkpoint.
nodes.output: A player-facing narrative history that respects visibility.

nodes.title: Story Remix Paths
nodes.summary: A completed story can be replayed through clearly labelled alternate routes that do not erase the canonical first run.
nodes.purpose: It supports curiosity and replay without forcing reset or loss of progress.
nodes.player_loop: Choose an archived branch, select a remix variant, review differences and play in a separate run context.
nodes.output: An additional branch record kept beside the original.

nodes.title: Vault Blueprint Library
nodes.summary: Every Vault is assembled from a versioned blueprint that states room order, rules, difficulty, solutions and exact rewards.
nodes.purpose: It makes challenge content testable and prevents a Vault from becoming a hidden random-reward box.
nodes.player_loop: Preview a blueprint, inspect its session length and solution policy, choose solo or party mode and enter.
nodes.output: A validated Vault definition with explicit versions and stable room IDs.

nodes.title: Puzzle Chambers
nodes.summary: A chamber contains one focused logic, spatial, word or deduction task with a verified solution path.
nodes.purpose: It gives the Vault a reusable unit of meaningful gameplay.
nodes.player_loop: Enter a chamber, inspect clues, submit a legal action, receive grounded feedback and open the next state when solved.
nodes.output: A solved chamber state and optional explanation.

nodes.title: Logic Key Mechanisms
nodes.summary: Keys are earned by solving visible sub-puzzles and open specific doors whose requirements are disclosed in advance.
nodes.purpose: It connects rooms without introducing consumable chance keys or surprise access costs.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect the door, identify its linked puzzle, solve the condition and use the persistent unlock.
nodes.output: A deterministic access flag tied to the Vault blueprint.

nodes.title: Relic Galleries
nodes.summary: A relic room presents curated lore artefacts and collection context as a discoverable gallery with exact completion criteria.
nodes.purpose: It ties Vault exploration to the Museum and story archive.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect the gallery, solve its access puzzle, read the provenance entry and record the discovery.
nodes.output: A fixed relic discovery and an archive reference.

nodes.title: Mastery Trial Rooms
nodes.summary: A trial tests a known mini-game or puzzle skill using a published difficulty and scoring rubric.
nodes.purpose: It links arcade mastery to adventure progress without giving random power rewards.
nodes.player_loop: Select a difficulty, review rules, complete the bounded trial and inspect the scoring breakdown.
nodes.output: A skill record, personal best and fixed completion recognition.

nodes.title: The Grand Mechanism
nodes.summary: A Vault finale is a multi-step logic encounter where the group coordinates switches, clues and turn-based choices.
nodes.purpose: It delivers a memorable climax without graphic violence or a requirement for frame-perfect action.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect the mechanism, assign roles, resolve each phase and use checkpoints before the final solution.
nodes.output: A completed finale state and a deterministic result summary.

nodes.title: Split-Path Chambers
nodes.summary: Different participants receive separate clues or mechanisms that must be combined to open a shared route.
nodes.purpose: It creates meaningful communication and makes each participant useful.
nodes.player_loop: Distribute roles, inspect individual clues privately, share permitted facts and commit a combined solution.
nodes.output: A party state containing private clue assignments and shared conclusions.

nodes.title: Vault Save Stones
nodes.summary: Explicit save stones record completed rooms, chosen routes and earned discoveries so a run can be resumed later.
nodes.purpose: It respects interrupted sessions and prevents progress loss from Discord disconnections.
nodes.player_loop: Reach a stone, inspect saved progress, pause or leave, then resume with the same blueprint version.
nodes.output: A recoverable checkpoint and idempotent room-completion history.

nodes.title: Fair Difficulty Profiles
nodes.summary: Difficulty profiles adjust clue density, allowed hints and puzzle complexity using documented, testable rules.
nodes.purpose: It supports different player skills without hidden adaptive difficulty or pressure.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a profile, preview its changes, start a clean run and switch only between runs.
nodes.output: A named rules profile and comparable score context.

nodes.title: Verified Puzzle Registry
nodes.summary: A registry stores known solutions, validation results, duplicate hashes and editorial approvals before a puzzle can be published.
nodes.purpose: It prevents unwinnable, ambiguous or accidentally duplicated challenge content.
nodes.player_loop: Submit a puzzle, run validators, review the solution count, approve a version and publish it to a Vault.
nodes.output: A validated puzzle asset with reproducible tests.

nodes.title: Field Gathering
nodes.summary: Players discover fixed resource nodes through map exploration, puzzle completion and authored route objectives.
nodes.purpose: It gives resources a clear origin and ties crafting to world knowledge rather than idle grinding.
nodes.player_loop: Visit a node, inspect its known requirements, complete the associated activity and claim its disclosed yield.
nodes.output: A provenance-marked resource batch with a known source.

nodes.title: The Recipe Codex
nodes.summary: A searchable book explains every discovered recipe, exact input quantities, output, tool requirements and alternate uses.
nodes.purpose: It removes guesswork from crafting and makes the economy understandable.
nodes.player_loop: Browse a recipe, inspect available inputs, pin it to a workbench and craft when ready.
nodes.output: A versioned recipe definition and a clear material plan.

nodes.title: The Maker's Workshop
nodes.summary: A shared workshop UI lets players queue one deterministic craft at a time, review its inputs and inspect the resulting item.
nodes.purpose: It centralises crafting rules and gives crafters a recognisable role.
nodes.player_loop: Select a recipe, reserve materials, confirm the cost, execute the recipe and inspect provenance.
nodes.output: A crafted item and an immutable input/output record.

nodes.title: Known Quality Grades
nodes.summary: Item quality comes from named, visible recipe conditions such as material grade or optional puzzle precision, not a hidden random roll.
nodes.purpose: It permits craft mastery while keeping outcomes reproducible.
nodes.player_loop: Review quality rules, select known inputs, satisfy the displayed condition and receive the corresponding grade.
nodes.output: A deterministic quality value with its rule version.

nodes.title: Commission Bench
nodes.summary: A crafter can accept a Bazaar work order with agreed inputs, fixed compensation and an explicit delivery contract.
nodes.purpose: It connects player skill and supply to real community demand.
nodes.player_loop: Review the order, accept terms, reserve inputs, craft, deliver and receive the exact settlement.
nodes.output: A completed commission and trade receipt.

nodes.title: Material Reclaim
nodes.summary: Unneeded eligible items can be converted into a published set of base materials using fixed recipes.
nodes.purpose: It reduces inventory clutter and gives obsolete items a useful path without destroying value unpredictably.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect reclaim output, choose eligible items, confirm the exact result and archive the conversion.
nodes.output: A deterministic material conversion record.

nodes.title: Workshop Repair
nodes.summary: Durable equipment can be restored using known materials and a published repair cost, without punitive breakage timers.
nodes.purpose: It gives equipment a maintenance role without forcing repetitive chores.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect an item's condition, view the full repair cost, confirm and restore its listed state.
nodes.output: A repair ledger entry and repaired item state.

nodes.title: Pattern and Set Assembly
nodes.summary: Several known components can combine into a decorative or functional set when the exact recipe is complete.
nodes.purpose: It creates long-range goals that link collections, crafting and homes.
nodes.player_loop: Review missing components, source them through play or trade, assemble the set and record the recipe.
nodes.output: A set item with deterministic contents and provenance.

nodes.title: Guild Workshop
nodes.summary: Guild members contribute approved materials to a shared project and use a published recipe to produce a community object.
nodes.purpose: It turns crafting into cooperative infrastructure rather than private inventory accumulation.
nodes.player_loop: Open the project, inspect contributions, add materials, reach the recipe threshold and execute once.
nodes.output: A guild-owned crafted output and contribution ledger.

nodes.title: Recipe Research
nodes.summary: Players can infer new recipes from authored clues and verified item relationships, then submit a solution for validation.
nodes.purpose: It makes crafting discovery a puzzle discipline instead of an RNG unlock.
nodes.player_loop: Collect references, propose a recipe, test against a bounded sandbox and publish only after validation.
nodes.output: A new versioned recipe with discoverer attribution.

nodes.title: The Grand Collection Index
nodes.summary: A searchable index records discovered relics, creatures, cards, recipes, cosmetics and authored content under stable IDs.
nodes.purpose: It creates one consistent collection model across every game and activity.
nodes.player_loop: Open the index, filter a category, inspect provenance, pin a set and follow a known discovery route.
nodes.output: A personal collection state and stable content references.

nodes.title: The Field Bestiary
nodes.summary: An illustrated bestiary records original creatures, habitats, traits, puzzle clues and non-graphic encounter rules.
nodes.purpose: It connects creature discovery to the Atlas, character abilities and story.
nodes.player_loop: Find a creature, complete its authored discovery condition, read its entry and record a new observation.
nodes.output: A bestiary entry with source region and verified facts.

nodes.title: The Relic Archive
nodes.summary: Relics are curated story objects with a known source, lore text, collection rule and display permissions.
nodes.purpose: It makes exploration rewards meaningful through history and context.
nodes.player_loop: Discover a relic, inspect its source, add it to the Archive and optionally display it.
nodes.output: A permanent relic record with provenance.

nodes.title: The Illustrated Compendium
nodes.summary: Collectible cards represent characters, landmarks, puzzles and authored scenes, with guaranteed sources and no random packs.
nodes.purpose: It offers a visual collection layer without loot boxes or chance-based tradable rewards.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect a card source, complete its listed activity, claim the exact card and add it to a set.
nodes.output: An account-bound or explicitly eligible card with documented origin.

nodes.title: The Museum Hall
nodes.summary: Players and guilds can arrange approved items and discoveries into themed exhibitions with clear authorship and visibility.
nodes.purpose: It gives collections a social purpose and turns personal progress into optional public storytelling.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a theme, select entries, arrange the display, preview permissions and publish or keep private.
nodes.output: A versioned exhibition that can be edited or removed by its owner.

nodes.title: Collection Sets
nodes.summary: Sets group related discoveries by theme, region or chapter and show exact missing entries and source activities.
nodes.purpose: It provides clear, attainable goals without hidden rarity odds.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a set, inspect each item source, complete optional activities and claim the fixed set completion mark.
nodes.output: A completed set record and non-power cosmetic recognition.

nodes.title: The Cosmetic Gallery
nodes.summary: A gallery organises earned palettes, frames, emotes and profile decorations while separating appearance from power.
nodes.purpose: It gives progression visible expression without pay-to-win effects.
nodes.player_loop: Preview a cosmetic, inspect its source, equip it or place it in a display and change it freely.
nodes.output: A cosmetic ownership flag and equipped appearance setting.

nodes.title: The Living Lore Index
nodes.summary: Lore entries link characters, factions, landmarks, items and chapters through citations to the actual game content.
nodes.purpose: It makes story comprehension cumulative and supports returning players.
nodes.player_loop: Open a lore topic, follow related nodes, inspect source chapters and save a reading path.
nodes.output: A graph of unlocked knowledge with provenance.

nodes.title: Collection Milestones
nodes.summary: Milestones recognise breadth, curation and exploration across sets rather than requiring one rare item drop.
nodes.purpose: It rewards varied participation and makes completion criteria legible.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect a milestone, see its required set of actions, complete them naturally and claim its fixed recognition.
nodes.output: An idempotent achievement tied to collection state.

nodes.title: Collector's Provenance View
nodes.summary: A detailed item history shows the recipe, quest or discovery that created an asset without exposing the private identity of previous holders.
nodes.purpose: It strengthens marketplace trust and protects legitimate earned ownership.
nodes.player_loop: Open an asset, inspect allowed origin records, verify its definition and return to the collection or Bazaar.
nodes.output: A privacy-filtered provenance chain and integrity reference.

nodes.title: The Pocket Arcade
nodes.summary: A visual catalogue presents approved games with rules, player count, expected session length, accessibility options and release status.
nodes.purpose: It makes Moonbyte's broad game library discoverable and helps players choose an experience that fits their time.
nodes.player_loop: Browse categories, compare game cards, preview rules and start a solo or multiplayer session.
nodes.output: A game selection and a validated session request.

nodes.title: Optional Daily Logic Desk
nodes.summary: A shared daily puzzle uses a published ruleset and lets anyone attempt it without streak loss or missed-day penalties.
nodes.purpose: It gives the community a common puzzle to discuss while keeping participation entirely optional.
nodes.player_loop: Open today's puzzle, inspect the rules, play at a chosen time and review the solution after completion.
nodes.output: A dated puzzle result and a personal best that does not decay.

nodes.title: The Practice School
nodes.summary: Each supported game can expose guided lessons, sample turns and progressively harder practice challenges.
nodes.purpose: It helps players learn rather than relying on unexplained losses or hidden difficulty.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a lesson, inspect the goal, try a guided example, practise independently and review the method.
nodes.output: A completed lesson record and recommended next difficulty.

nodes.title: Puzzle Generator and Validator
nodes.summary: A deterministic generator produces puzzles only when a solution validator confirms their solvability and intended difficulty.
nodes.purpose: It creates scalable content without publishing broken or ambiguous puzzles.
nodes.player_loop: Request a puzzle profile, generate from a versioned seed, validate the solution and publish only approved content.
nodes.output: A verified puzzle instance and reproducible solution key.

nodes.title: The Party Game Shelf
nodes.summary: Fast social games share the same lobby, turn ownership, scoring and leave controls rather than inventing unique multiplayer plumbing.
nodes.purpose: It makes the Arcade feel cohesive and reduces bugs across multiple titles.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a party game, invite participants, ready the table, play a bounded round and show a result.
nodes.output: A completed party session and shared summary.

nodes.title: Asynchronous Challenge Cards
nodes.summary: Players can send a friend a defined puzzle or score challenge that can be completed independently within a generous window.
nodes.purpose: It supports friends in different time zones without a live-session requirement.
nodes.player_loop: Create a challenge from a supported game, share a link, complete one attempt and compare verified scores.
nodes.output: A paired challenge record with deterministic comparison rules.

nodes.title: Friendly Arcade League
nodes.summary: An opt-in league groups comparable scores across a fixed rules version and gives participants a clear way to leave or hide results.
nodes.purpose: It adds structured competition without prizes, entry fees or daily attendance pressure.
nodes.player_loop: Join a league, inspect ranking rules, play during the published period and review final standings.
nodes.output: A rules-versioned score table and cosmetic recognition only.

nodes.title: Replay and Review Desk
nodes.summary: A replay view reconstructs legal actions and key decisions for supported turn-based games without exposing hidden player information.
nodes.purpose: It helps players learn from a match and creates useful shared moments.
nodes.player_loop: Open a completed match, choose an allowed perspective, step through actions and inspect the rule explanation.
nodes.output: A redacted action replay tied to a match version.

nodes.title: Arcade Control Profiles
nodes.summary: Games expose named control profiles for simplified inputs, longer thinking windows, text-only boards and reduced-motion presentation.
nodes.purpose: It lets more people participate on Discord without requiring fast reactions or precise timing.
nodes.player_loop: Preview a profile, apply it before a match, check supported modes and retain the preference.
nodes.output: A per-player input preference with game compatibility metadata.

nodes.title: Curated Game Routes
nodes.summary: A playlist links several games around a theme, estimated total time and optional transitions rather than demanding an endless session.
nodes.purpose: It creates guided discovery and lets communities run compact themed nights.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a playlist, inspect every included game, launch one step, finish or skip, then stop at any point.
nodes.output: A completed playlist path and optional recap.

nodes.title: Universal Lobby Contract
nodes.summary: A single lobby system handles visibility, host identity, seat limits, invitations, readiness and launch conditions for every multiplayer game.
nodes.purpose: It prevents game-specific invitation bugs and makes lobbies familiar across Moonbyte.
nodes.player_loop: Create a lobby, choose privacy, invite or admit players, inspect the rule preview and launch when valid.
nodes.output: A versioned lobby state and membership list.

nodes.title: Party Formation Desk
nodes.summary: Players can create a temporary party, invite known friends and carry the group between compatible activities.
nodes.purpose: It makes cooperation persist across games without inventing a public matchmaking pressure loop.
nodes.player_loop: Create a party, review membership, choose a destination, confirm availability and enter a session together.
nodes.output: A temporary party identity with explicit membership and exit controls.

nodes.title: Friend-First Match Finder
nodes.summary: The match finder prioritises invited friends and clearly labelled public rooms, with skill grouping only where a game needs it.
nodes.purpose: It helps players find a match without dark patterns or opaque engagement ranking.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a game and mode, inspect queue visibility, join or cancel, then accept a compatible lobby.
nodes.output: A match proposal with visible constraints and cancellation state.

nodes.title: Shared Turn Engine
nodes.summary: Turn-based games use one engine for actor ownership, legal action validation, phase changes and stale interaction rejection.
nodes.purpose: It gives every game a tested foundation and protects against button races.
nodes.player_loop: Receive the turn, inspect legal actions, submit one action, receive authoritative resolution and pass control.
nodes.output: A canonical turn event and versioned game state.

nodes.title: Simultaneous Choice Windows
nodes.summary: Selected games collect sealed choices from all participants before resolving the phase using a published rule order.
nodes.purpose: It enables strategic group play without frame-based real-time networking.
nodes.player_loop: Open a phase, submit a private choice, revise before lock, resolve once and show a shared summary.
nodes.output: A sealed phase record with deterministic resolution.

nodes.title: Spectator Gallery
nodes.summary: Hosts can enable read-only spectators for supported public games with deliberate information redaction.
nodes.purpose: It allows community viewing without giving spectators control or exposing hidden hands and roles.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect spectator policy, join as view-only, receive public board updates and leave independently.
nodes.output: A spectator permission and filtered view model.

nodes.title: Friendly Tournament Brackets
nodes.summary: A bracket organises opt-in matches with clear seeds, tie rules and schedules but no pooled stakes or cash-equivalent prizes.
nodes.purpose: It provides tournament structure while respecting Moonbyte's no-wagering boundary.
nodes.player_loop: Create a bracket, publish rules, register teams, play each round and archive the final results.
nodes.output: A deterministic bracket and cosmetic achievement record.

nodes.title: Shared Cooperative Boards
nodes.summary: A cooperative board lets players contribute legal actions toward one group objective with visible contribution attribution.
nodes.purpose: It makes collaboration more than parallel solo play.
nodes.player_loop: Create a group board, assign or choose a task, submit an action, inspect shared state and resolve the objective.
nodes.output: A shared board state with a contribution timeline.

nodes.title: Reconnect and Rejoin
nodes.summary: A reconnect path restores a participant to a valid session state after app reload, network interruption or Discord message replacement.
nodes.purpose: It prevents accidental session loss and reduces reliance on one live interaction.
nodes.player_loop: Reopen the session, authenticate through Discord context, inspect the saved phase and rejoin if permitted.
nodes.output: A recovered participant state with stale-action protection.

nodes.title: Table Votes and Host Controls
nodes.summary: A bounded host toolkit handles start, pause, continue, kick, transfer-host and cancellation under clear permission rules.
nodes.purpose: It makes group sessions manageable without allowing one participant to silently rewrite outcomes.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect the current phase, choose an allowed host action, confirm consequential changes and record the event.
nodes.output: An auditable host action and explicit session transition.

nodes.title: Player Character Sheet
nodes.summary: A character sheet collects a chosen name, visual identity, archetype, equipped options and a concise adventure summary.
nodes.purpose: It provides a consistent role-playing identity without demanding extensive personal data.
nodes.player_loop: Create a character, choose permitted options, preview the sheet and save a versioned profile.
nodes.output: A player-owned character record separate from Discord account credentials.

nodes.title: Archetype Codex
nodes.summary: A small set of original archetypes defines different tactical approaches such as Navigator, Maker, Scholar and Guardian.
nodes.purpose: It gives players meaningful starting choices without creating a strict class hierarchy.
nodes.player_loop: Compare archetypes, inspect active and passive rules, choose one and test it in practice.
nodes.output: A documented archetype with versioned rules and respec clarity.

nodes.title: Skill Path Map
nodes.summary: A branching skill map offers side-grade abilities and utility unlocks with visible prerequisites and no paid shortcuts.
nodes.purpose: It supports long-term mastery while avoiding a single mandatory build.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect a path, review all branches, earn a milestone, choose an unlock and test it in a supported game.
nodes.output: A character progression flag and a documented ability selection.

nodes.title: Adventure Loadouts
nodes.summary: Players can save several named combinations of role, equipment and utility choices for different game categories.
nodes.purpose: It reduces repeated setup and makes preparation part of strategy.
nodes.player_loop: Build a loadout, validate its compatibility, save, select before a session and revise between runs.
nodes.output: A versioned preset with no hidden inventory transfer.

nodes.title: Companion Chronicle
nodes.summary: Original non-player companions have authored abilities, history and optional support interactions rather than random gacha acquisition.
nodes.purpose: It creates attachment through story and utility without paid pulls or scarcity pressure.
nodes.player_loop: Meet through a known story path, review companion rules, choose a support role and save their current assignment.
nodes.output: An account-bound companion record and known unlock source.

nodes.title: Role Synergy Board
nodes.summary: The board explains useful combinations of party roles and provides alternative solutions so one role is never mandatory.
nodes.purpose: It rewards communication and varied approaches rather than enforcing a single build.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect a challenge, compare role tools, select a combination and resolve the group objective.
nodes.output: A synergy hint set and party composition snapshot.

nodes.title: Equipment Ledger
nodes.summary: Equipment gives transparent utility effects, provenance and compatibility rules, with no random stat rolls.
nodes.purpose: It connects crafting and strategy without turning the Bazaar into a power arms race.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect an item, compare exact effects, equip before a run and track its source.
nodes.output: A character equipment state backed by item definitions.

nodes.title: Titles and Identity Marks
nodes.summary: Titles display authored achievements, roles and creative contributions with player-controlled visibility.
nodes.purpose: It lets players express identity without comparing raw playtime or wealth.
nodes.player_loop: Browse eligible titles, inspect their source, equip one and hide it whenever desired.
nodes.output: An earned title flag and profile presentation setting.

nodes.title: Pixel Persona Studio
nodes.summary: A bounded creator combines original approved palettes, outfit parts and accessories into a personal pixel character.
nodes.purpose: It gives the world a visual identity and makes cosmetic creation accessible.
nodes.player_loop: Choose parts, preview scale and contrast, save a draft and publish only the final selected appearance.
nodes.output: A validated appearance recipe and reusable avatar render input.

nodes.title: Non-Combat Talents
nodes.summary: Utility talents support navigation, clue interpretation, crafting and social coordination rather than increasing damage or competitive power.
nodes.purpose: It gives different characters useful identities in non-combat play.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a talent, inspect its supported activities, use it in a valid context and review its effect.
nodes.output: A character ability event and a transparent rules effect.

nodes.title: Experience and Milestone Ledger
nodes.summary: Experience is awarded by documented game actions with reasonable caps and no incentive to remain online indefinitely.
nodes.purpose: It provides a common sense of progress across mini-games and longer adventures.
nodes.player_loop: Complete an eligible activity, preview its award, receive one idempotent event and inspect the progress ledger.
nodes.output: A player experience total derived from immutable award records.

nodes.title: Skill Mastery Tracks
nodes.summary: Each major game category has a mastery track that recognises learning, varied play and improved decisions.
nodes.purpose: It lets players specialise and see progress without one global level dominating every activity.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a track, inspect milestones, play a supported activity and claim its known recognition.
nodes.output: A category-specific mastery state and achievement references.

nodes.title: Achievement Registry
nodes.summary: Achievements have explicit triggers, versioned criteria, evidence sources and clear display settings.
nodes.purpose: It turns accomplishments into trustworthy records that can be tested and audited.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect an achievement, complete its stated condition, verify evidence and receive the idempotent unlock.
nodes.output: A stable achievement record with source event and rules version.

nodes.title: Player Honour Record
nodes.summary: A privacy-safe record recognises helpful play, fulfilled agreements and positive community contributions with appeal paths.
nodes.purpose: It gives social trust an evidence basis without turning popularity into power.
nodes.player_loop: Receive an eligible commendation, review its policy, inspect aggregate evidence and request correction if wrong.
nodes.output: A non-transferable reputation summary with moderation safeguards.

nodes.title: Personal Milestone Contracts
nodes.summary: Players can choose a bounded mastery objective such as learning a new puzzle type or completing a co-op role.
nodes.purpose: It gives self-directed goals without punishing players for abandoning them.
nodes.player_loop: Browse optional contracts, choose one, inspect completion conditions, make progress and stop or swap freely.
nodes.output: A player-selected contract with no expiry penalty.

nodes.title: Milestone Route Planner
nodes.summary: A planner shows several valid ways to progress toward a selected achievement or skill unlock.
nodes.purpose: It turns long-term goals into clear choices and avoids undisclosed grind requirements.
nodes.player_loop: Pick a milestone, compare its valid routes, pin one route and complete any eligible path.
nodes.output: A saved plan and transparent progress estimate.

nodes.title: Earned Cosmetic Unlocks
nodes.summary: Cosmetics unlock through authored achievements, collections, community works and predictable milestones.
nodes.purpose: It makes visible rewards meaningful without creating gameplay advantages.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect a cosmetic source, complete its condition, claim the unlock and equip or hide it.
nodes.output: An account-bound cosmetic entitlement with provenance.

nodes.title: Skill Badge Portfolio
nodes.summary: Badges summarise demonstrated ability in a specific rules version and are never traded or purchased.
nodes.purpose: It gives players a portable record of mastery without claiming a broad measure of personal worth.
nodes.player_loop: Complete a verified assessment, inspect its scope, display the badge if desired and update after later versions.
nodes.output: A scoped skill badge with testable evidence.

nodes.title: Personal Best Registry
nodes.summary: Personal records store the best supported metric for each game alongside the rules version and difficulty.
nodes.purpose: It supports improvement without comparing players who used incompatible conditions.
nodes.player_loop: Finish a round, inspect the metric, compare like-for-like attempts and save a new best when earned.
nodes.output: A personal record with immutable result reference.

nodes.title: Account-Bound Recognition
nodes.summary: Special recognition rewards remain attached to the earning player and are excluded from the Bazaar by definition.
nodes.purpose: It prevents achievements from being converted into trade pressure or status farming.
nodes.player_loop: Complete the stated milestone, receive an account-bound mark and view its source in the profile.
nodes.output: A non-transferable achievement reward with anti-duplication tests.

nodes.title: World Fairs
nodes.summary: A festival groups mini-games, story scenes, crafting recipes and shared decorations under one authored theme.
nodes.purpose: It provides a celebratory reason to explore multiple systems without a timed reward trap.
nodes.player_loop: Open the fair, inspect activities and durations, choose one station and return later without loss.
nodes.output: A festival progress record and permanent archive of completed content.

nodes.title: Seasonal Story Chapters
nodes.summary: A chapter release adds a new narrative arc and map content while older chapters remain available to new players.
nodes.purpose: It creates a living story without forcing simultaneous attendance.
nodes.player_loop: Read the chapter description, choose a starting point, play at a personal pace and archive the ending.
nodes.output: A versioned chapter state and accessible replay route.

nodes.title: Server Celebration Kits
nodes.summary: Administrators can assemble approved event schedules, party tables, quizzes and decoration options for their community.
nodes.purpose: It makes Moonbyte adaptable to a server's culture and moderation needs.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a kit, preview its content, set channel rules, publish the event and close it cleanly.
nodes.output: A guild-owned event configuration with scoped permissions.

nodes.title: World Restoration Projects
nodes.summary: A shared project lets players contribute puzzle solutions, crafted objects or discoveries to a permanent world improvement.
nodes.purpose: It makes the wider world react to community activity with a durable outcome.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect a project, choose a contribution path, submit valid work and view the published world change.
nodes.output: A global project milestone and world-state event.

nodes.title: Puzzle Rotation Archive
nodes.summary: A featured puzzle changes on a documented schedule while previous puzzles remain available in an archive.
nodes.purpose: It keeps discovery fresh without making a missed day or week punitive.
nodes.player_loop: Open the featured puzzle, inspect its date and rules, play now or choose an archived version.
nodes.output: A dated puzzle instance and persistent archive entry.

nodes.title: The Celebration Wall
nodes.summary: A shared board highlights completed guild projects, player creativity and milestone achievements with visibility controls.
nodes.purpose: It shifts celebrations toward meaningful contribution instead of raw attendance totals.
