nodes.player_loop: Choose a verified event, preview its attribution, publish to an allowed audience and archive it.
nodes.output: A public-safe celebration entry.

nodes.title: Neighbourhood Festival Circuit
nodes.summary: Independent servers can opt into a shared puzzle or art theme while keeping configuration and user data separate.
nodes.purpose: It gives Moonbyte a wider community feel without merging private server records.
nodes.player_loop: Review the public event rules, opt in at guild level, submit a valid result and view the aggregate public outcome.
nodes.output: A cross-server event result with no shared private profile data.

nodes.title: Open Archive Routes
nodes.summary: Every festival or chapter has a later access route for players who were absent during its original presentation.
nodes.purpose: It removes pressure to log in on a schedule and protects content longevity.
nodes.player_loop: Browse the archive, inspect what is still playable, start a preserved activity and keep the resulting record.
nodes.output: An evergreen content link and versioned archive state.

nodes.title: Festival Chronicle
nodes.summary: The chronicle stores festival artwork, completed puzzles, authored stories and community summaries after an event ends.
nodes.purpose: It turns temporary presentation into lasting community history.
nodes.player_loop: Select an event, browse its sections, follow content links and add an original recap if permitted.
nodes.output: A permanent event archive with attribution.

nodes.title: Moonbyte Anniversary
nodes.summary: An anniversary celebration looks back at the world's history, community projects and game milestones without resetting progress.
nodes.purpose: It creates a shared moment of reflection rather than an exclusive reward race.
nodes.player_loop: Open the anniversary page, view personal and server memories, play optional retrospective games and close it.
nodes.output: A dated celebration archive and cosmetic recognition that is not power.

nodes.title: Personal Home Plot
nodes.summary: Each player receives a simple personal space with a few themed areas that can be arranged using earned objects.
nodes.purpose: It creates a calm long-term destination that expresses progress without requiring constant maintenance.
nodes.player_loop: Open the home, choose an area, place an owned decoration, preview and save the layout.
nodes.output: A personal layout state and an accessible text inventory.

nodes.title: Room Layout Studio
nodes.summary: A grid-based editor lets players position approved furniture and pixel art within bounded, mobile-friendly controls.
nodes.purpose: It offers creative expression without relying on frame-perfect drag interactions.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a room, select an object, place or rotate it, validate the grid and save a draft or publish it.
nodes.output: A versioned layout recipe with collision and bounds validation.

nodes.title: Display Shelves
nodes.summary: Shelves expose selected collectibles and achievements to permitted visitors while leaving the rest of the inventory private.
nodes.purpose: It turns a collection into a story without publishing ownership by default.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a shelf, select entries, set visibility, preview the result and invite visitors if desired.
nodes.output: A display configuration separate from inventory ownership.

nodes.title: The Pocket Garden
nodes.summary: A garden uses deterministic planting and optional puzzle-based tending to create decorations and lore, with no decay for absence.
nodes.purpose: It provides a gentle crafting loop without idle timers or punitive harvest windows.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a plant, inspect its recipe, complete an optional care activity and collect when convenient.
nodes.output: A persistent garden state with non-decaying progress.

nodes.title: Home Workshop Extension
nodes.summary: Players can place a crafted workshop station that provides a more convenient view of existing recipes and loadouts.
nodes.purpose: It links crafting to personal space without granting hidden production multipliers.
nodes.player_loop: Craft or earn a station, place it, inspect its supported recipes and launch the standard workshop service.
nodes.output: A home station configuration that references canonical recipes.

nodes.title: Companion Nook
nodes.summary: A home area displays companions already earned through story content and lets players choose a current non-combat appearance.
nodes.purpose: It provides a visual home for original companions without paid acquisition or neglect mechanics.
nodes.player_loop: Select an owned companion, preview its display pose, set visibility and save the room.
nodes.output: A cosmetic companion display with no decay or feeding timer.

nodes.title: Decorative Collections
nodes.summary: Decor sets group furnishings by region, story or event and show exact item sources and missing pieces.
nodes.purpose: It combines crafting and collections into a clear home-building goal.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a set, inspect its recipe sources, craft or discover pieces and arrange them in the room.
nodes.output: A completed decor set and optional display achievement.

nodes.title: Friend Visit Rooms
nodes.summary: Players can create a visit link with explicit guest permissions and a short-lived view scope for their home.
nodes.purpose: It supports social expression without opening private inventory or unsolicited visits.
nodes.player_loop: Choose guest access, create a room visit, let invited friends view permitted areas and close access at any time.
nodes.output: A visit session with explicit scope and audit-safe access expiry.

nodes.title: Shared Neighbourhood Square
nodes.summary: A guild or server can curate a shared public square with contributed decorations and community project displays.
nodes.purpose: It creates a common space connected to guild projects and festivals.
nodes.player_loop: Open the square, inspect its project, submit an eligible decoration and review publication permissions.
nodes.output: A guild-scoped shared layout and contributor record.

nodes.title: Home Design Snapshots
nodes.summary: Players can save named layout snapshots, compare changes and restore an earlier approved arrangement.
nodes.purpose: It makes creative editing reversible and reduces fear of losing work.
nodes.player_loop: Save a snapshot, make changes, preview the diff and restore any retained version.
nodes.output: A versioned layout history with owner-controlled retention.

nodes.title: Puzzle Studio
nodes.summary: Players can compose puzzles from approved templates with clues, answer rules, difficulty labels and validation tests.
nodes.purpose: It invites community creativity while preventing ambiguous or impossible puzzles from entering public play.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a template, enter original clues, run local validation, preview text and submit for review.
nodes.output: A draft puzzle package and validation report.

nodes.title: Quest Workshop
nodes.summary: An authoring tool creates short branching stories from constrained scenes, conditions and original dialogue blocks.
nodes.purpose: It expands narrative content without allowing arbitrary scripts or untrusted code execution.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a story template, connect scenes, define conditions, preview all branches and submit for review.
nodes.output: A versioned quest graph with author attribution.

nodes.title: Vault Layout Workshop
nodes.summary: Creators can arrange supported chamber types, clue placements and published reward definitions into a testable Vault draft.
nodes.purpose: It makes challenge design extensible while keeping room logic within approved contracts.
nodes.player_loop: Select chambers, wire legal exits, run solution validation, test the complete route and submit the blueprint.
nodes.output: A Vault draft with solvability evidence.

nodes.title: Game Rule Templates
nodes.summary: A template library exposes safe configuration knobs for supported game variants without allowing players to rewrite authoritative code.
nodes.purpose: It permits variation while keeping the Rust engine's rules and permissions in control.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a supported template, edit bounded options, run compatibility checks and publish a private playtest.
nodes.output: A schema-validated variant definition.

nodes.title: Original Card Set Builder
nodes.summary: A card-set editor creates original thematic collections with fixed sources and non-random acquisition rules.
nodes.purpose: It adds collection identity without cloning protected card games or using paid pack mechanics.
nodes.player_loop: Choose approved card layouts, author original descriptions, define guaranteed unlock sources and submit the set.
nodes.output: A content pack with provenance and deterministic unlock conditions.

nodes.title: Pixel Sticker Workshop
nodes.summary: A bounded pixel editor lets users design small original stickers or room decorations using a limited palette and grid.
nodes.purpose: It gives the visual world a community art pipeline with predictable output constraints.
nodes.player_loop: Select a canvas size, draw with accessible controls, validate the palette and export a moderated draft.
nodes.output: An original raster asset with dimensions and attribution.

nodes.title: Community Playtest Queue
nodes.summary: Creators can invite opt-in testers to a private draft session and collect structured feedback without public ranking.
nodes.purpose: It improves content quality and tests edge cases before publication.
nodes.player_loop: Submit a draft, set the tester scope, run a bounded playtest, record feedback and revise the version.
nodes.output: A private test report and draft revision history.

nodes.title: Content Review Pipeline
nodes.summary: Every public creation passes automated validation and a human review path appropriate to its content and visibility.
nodes.purpose: It protects players from spam, copied material and unsafe submissions.
nodes.player_loop: Check metadata, run validators, review reports, approve or request edits and record the decision.
nodes.output: A moderation state, reviewer reason and publication gate.

nodes.title: Creator Credit Ledger
nodes.summary: Approved content includes original author credit, version, source assets and permitted reuse terms.
nodes.purpose: It builds trust and encourages original work without confusing ownership.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect a content package, verify its author and assets, accept the listed use terms and publish with attribution.
nodes.output: A provenance record and a clear rights statement.

nodes.title: Community Pack Publishing
nodes.summary: Approved puzzles, stories, decorations and event kits can be grouped into discoverable packs with explicit compatibility.
nodes.purpose: It makes good community content reusable across servers without bypassing moderation.
nodes.player_loop: Select approved entries, declare dependencies, preview the pack, publish a version and track corrections.
nodes.output: A versioned content pack with safe dependency metadata.

nodes.title: Published Rulebooks
nodes.summary: Every competitive game has a public rules version, legal-action definition, scoring model and tie resolution.
nodes.purpose: It lets players understand what counts before competing and prevents silent changes.
nodes.player_loop: Open a game card, inspect the current rules version, compare revisions and start only after the terms are clear.
nodes.output: A versioned rulebook linked to sessions and replays.

nodes.title: Commit and Reveal Service
nodes.summary: Eligible randomised score-only sessions can publish a SHA-512 commitment before play and reveal the seed and transcript afterward.
nodes.purpose: It enables independent verification while keeping cryptographic hashing distinct from entropy generation.
nodes.player_loop: Generate OS-backed secret entropy, publish commitment, freeze inputs, derive result with unbiased mapping and reveal transcript.
nodes.output: A verifiable transcript with documented derivation and no economy payout.

nodes.title: Scoring Contract Registry
nodes.summary: Each score metric declares its inputs, range, aggregation, tie handling and supported rules versions.
nodes.purpose: It prevents leaderboards from comparing unlike sessions or hidden score changes.
nodes.player_loop: Resolve a match, calculate from canonical events, apply the declared tie rule and save the score evidence.
nodes.output: A deterministic score record and rules reference.

nodes.title: Optional Skill Rating
nodes.summary: A rating model can estimate competitive skill for compatible game modes while exposing uncertainty and allowing players to opt out.
nodes.purpose: It creates fairer match groupings without presenting rating as personal worth or a universal ranking.
nodes.player_loop: Play eligible matches, update using a documented model, inspect uncertainty and hide or reset the visible rating where supported.
nodes.output: A bounded rating record and model version.

nodes.title: Match Review Transcript
nodes.summary: Participants can inspect a redacted timeline of accepted actions, phase changes, score calculations and disconnect handling.
nodes.purpose: It gives players evidence when a result is questioned and supports learning.
nodes.player_loop: Open a match, choose public-safe details, compare events with the rulebook and request review if inconsistent.
nodes.output: A replayable audit timeline with private information filtered.

nodes.title: Integrity Guardrails
nodes.summary: Rate limits, action idempotency, anomaly flags and transaction constraints prevent duplicate rewards and exploit loops.
nodes.purpose: It protects player trust without invasive behavioural profiling.
nodes.player_loop: Validate a request, check only necessary counters, reject unsafe duplicates and record a minimal reason code.
nodes.output: A bounded integrity event and safe rejection response.

nodes.title: Tournament Rules Desk
nodes.summary: Tournament organisers configure bracket size, match format, dispute window and cosmetic recognition under one published policy.
nodes.purpose: It supports structured play without entry fees, cash prizes, stakes or pooled currency.
nodes.player_loop: Publish rules, register teams, schedule matches, resolve rounds and archive the final bracket.
nodes.output: A deterministic tournament record with no wager or prize-pool data model.

nodes.title: Leaderboard Integrity
nodes.summary: A leaderboard stores score provenance, rules version, eligible mode and tie policy alongside each displayed result.
nodes.purpose: It makes rankings explainable and robust against forged or incomparable submissions.
nodes.player_loop: Select a scope, filter compatible results, inspect the rules and report a specific record for review.
nodes.output: A rules-consistent leaderboard snapshot.

nodes.title: Equal Conditions Profiles
nodes.summary: Supported competitive games can constrain optional assists to equivalent modes or report them as separate categories.
nodes.purpose: It keeps comparisons fair while preserving accessibility options for everyone.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a mode, inspect allowed assists, confirm the profile and compare only against the same rules category.
nodes.output: A mode classification and accessible comparison contract.

nodes.title: Result Appeal Desk
nodes.summary: A participant can request a review of a specific match result with a reason code and linked evidence.
nodes.purpose: It adds accountability without automatically overturning a result through popularity or pressure.
nodes.player_loop: Select a result, identify the disputed rule, submit evidence, receive a review state and inspect the decision.
nodes.output: A private appeal record and reasoned resolution.

nodes.title: Friend Circle
nodes.summary: Players can maintain a private list of known Moonbyte friends with clear invitation, block and removal controls.
nodes.purpose: It supports repeat cooperation without a public social graph or unsolicited contact surface.
nodes.player_loop: Send an invitation through an allowed Discord context, accept or decline, choose sharing scope and revoke anytime.
nodes.output: A minimal friendship relation with explicit visibility settings.

nodes.title: Cooperative Role Planner
nodes.summary: A party can assign optional roles such as clue keeper, map reader, builder and coordinator before a shared session.
nodes.purpose: It helps groups divide work and makes quieter contributions visible.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect the activity, choose a role, review its actions, change before launch and contribute during the session.
nodes.output: A party role map linked to the session.

nodes.title: Opt-In Mentor Sessions
nodes.summary: Experienced players can host short lessons for a chosen game with an explicit topic and no follower or popularity reward.
nodes.purpose: It supports learning while avoiding pressure, unsolicited messaging and hierarchy abuse.
nodes.player_loop: Publish a lesson slot, allow interested players to opt in, run the practice session and close invitations.
nodes.output: A lesson record and structured feedback with blocking/reporting controls.

nodes.title: Interest Clubs
nodes.summary: Players can join small opt-in clubs around puzzles, cartography, crafting, stories or particular games.
nodes.purpose: It creates social discovery beyond a single server while keeping membership visible only as chosen.
nodes.player_loop: Browse club rules, preview its scope, request membership, join and leave from one control.
nodes.output: A club membership with moderation and privacy settings.

nodes.title: Thoughtful Gift Exchange
nodes.summary: Players may send eligible account-safe cosmetics or low-impact crafted items under strict frequency and provenance rules.
nodes.purpose: It supports generosity without currency farming or a cash-equivalent gift market.
nodes.player_loop: Choose an eligible gift, inspect recipient and item, confirm once and provide a receipt to both parties.
nodes.output: A one-way gift record with duplicate and self-gift protections.

nodes.title: Community Message Board
nodes.summary: A bounded in-world mailbox carries structured invitations, trade notices and shared activity recaps instead of unrestricted direct messaging.
nodes.purpose: It keeps social interactions useful and reduces abuse surfaces.
nodes.player_loop: Open a notice, choose its structured action, respond through the original feature and archive it.
nodes.output: A typed notification record with expiry and mute controls.

nodes.title: Positive Contribution Notes
nodes.summary: Players can recognise a specific helpful action such as explaining a puzzle or coordinating a group, subject to rate limits.
nodes.purpose: It reinforces useful behaviour without converting reactions into tradable currency or popularity scores.
nodes.player_loop: Select a verified session, choose a specific note, preview public visibility and submit or cancel.
nodes.output: A privacy-controlled commendation linked to an evidence event.

nodes.title: Shared Session Memories
nodes.summary: After a group activity, participants can save a recap containing allowed events, screenshots or authored notes where rights permit.
nodes.purpose: It gives multiplayer sessions a social afterlife and links to the guild chronicle.
nodes.player_loop: Finish a session, choose shareable moments, approve visibility and save a group memory.
nodes.output: A shared memory record with participant controls.

nodes.title: Friend Discovery Routes
nodes.summary: Players can discover new games through a friend's opt-in public activity card rather than tracking private presence.
nodes.purpose: It makes recommendations social while preserving the choice not to broadcast play.
nodes.player_loop: Open a shared card, inspect the activity, start privately or request an invite and hide future shares if desired.
nodes.output: A non-invasive shared recommendation event.

nodes.title: Social Boundaries Panel
nodes.summary: A player can control invites, visits, friend requests, mentions and shared-content visibility from one consistent settings area.
nodes.purpose: It makes safety controls discoverable across every social system.
nodes.player_loop: Open boundaries, inspect defaults, choose audience and notification rules, block or revoke and review the change.
nodes.output: A central preference set checked by social services.

nodes.title: Universal Control Profiles
nodes.summary: A shared preference layer standardises keyboard, Discord button, text-only and extended-time controls across supported games.
nodes.purpose: It prevents each game from inventing different accessibility behaviour.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a profile, inspect compatible features, preview controls and apply preferences before sessions.
nodes.output: A validated player control profile and game compatibility map.

nodes.title: Visual Comfort Settings
nodes.summary: Players can select high contrast, reduced motion, simpler animation and readable text density for supported views.
nodes.purpose: It makes the full-colour pixel-art world usable across different devices and sensitivities.
nodes.player_loop: Open display settings, preview each option, apply a combination and retain the preference across surfaces.
nodes.output: A display preference set shared by Discord renderers and the React Activity.

nodes.title: Language and Locale Registry
nodes.summary: Text content can carry locale identifiers, fallbacks and review status so new languages do not silently ship as machine-quality text.
nodes.purpose: It lets the world grow internationally while keeping rules and legal actions unambiguous.
nodes.player_loop: Choose a locale, inspect translation coverage, use reviewed strings and report a missing or unclear phrase.
nodes.output: A locale preference and versioned translation catalogue.

nodes.title: Text-First Play Mode
nodes.summary: Every visual board and important state has a compact text representation with labels for actions and current status.
nodes.purpose: It ensures that the game remains playable when images fail or a player prefers text.
nodes.player_loop: Enable text mode, open a game board, read the state, submit the same legal action and view the result.
nodes.output: A text view model generated from the same authoritative state.

nodes.title: Moderator Console
nodes.summary: A least-privilege moderation surface handles reports, content review, session safety and server settings without exposing private inventory.
nodes.purpose: It gives moderators enough information to protect a server without granting database-wide access.
nodes.player_loop: Open a scoped queue, inspect minimal evidence, choose a bounded action, record the reason and close the case.
nodes.output: An auditable moderation action with role and scope checks.

nodes.title: Report and Review Pipeline
nodes.summary: Players can report public content, trade issues and social behaviour through structured categories and clear status updates.
nodes.purpose: It creates a consistent path to help while avoiding public pile-ons or unbounded evidence collection.
nodes.player_loop: Choose the offending object, select a reason, submit privately, check case status and appeal where supported.
nodes.output: A private report record with evidence retention limits.

nodes.title: Privacy and Data Center
nodes.summary: A central privacy command and Activity page show stored categories, purpose, export and deletion status honestly.
nodes.purpose: It makes privacy a usable product feature rather than a paragraph hidden in documentation.
nodes.player_loop: Inspect data inventory, request export, review deletion scope, confirm as the owner and receive a truthful result.
nodes.output: A privacy request state and complete repository coverage map.

nodes.title: Quiet Notification Rules
nodes.summary: A preference engine applies opt-in topics, quiet hours, frequency caps and immediate mute across reminders and digests.
nodes.purpose: It keeps Discord useful without nagging, forced attendance or hidden notification defaults.
nodes.player_loop: Choose topics and timing, preview the effect, pause or mute globally and change settings later.
nodes.output: A versioned notification policy checked before every delivery.

nodes.title: Session Reliability Desk
nodes.summary: Operational state tracks gateway health, session recovery, SQLite contention, render failures and retry outcomes without collecting message content.
nodes.purpose: It prevents infrastructure failures from becoming player progress loss.
nodes.player_loop: Detect a fault, preserve durable state, retry idempotently, notify only when useful and expose a safe status.
nodes.output: A bounded health snapshot and recovery event stream.

nodes.title: World Content Policy
nodes.summary: A shared policy defines age-appropriate text, original asset rights, user-content review and disallowed content across all modules.
nodes.purpose: It lets a large content catalogue grow without inconsistent moderation decisions.
nodes.player_loop: Check a content source, validate text and asset rights, apply review status and block unapproved public publication.
nodes.output: A policy version and content eligibility result.
